title: Checks for theOS's apps: the crawl and the docs check
note: The first AIP of avenCEO's new sequence: avenCEO is built with its own steps, by hand, before any of it is automated. The 91 current intents (theOS/docs/intents.json, numbered OLD-AIP-1 to OLD-AIP-91) are consolidated into this format later, in their own AIP.

who: Samuel, the one person who decides, whose attention is the scarcest resource.
The agents that do the work: each AIP starts the ones its work needs, and several AIPs can run at once, each with its own (D-26).
Anyone who later needs to know why something is the way it is.
problem.experience: Samuel catches problems the agents should have caught, and repeats corrections.

items.text: The intent detail page broke: two parts of the page shared one CSS class name.
The scenario table squeezed its first column into a tall strip.
The intents and decisions pages did not scroll.
The board scrolled as a whole instead of per column.
Not every "rule" was renamed to "policy" after that was decided.
Slides kept an old shape of operations after its single source of truth changed.
The published page was not updated after a change.

evidence.group: Judgement, which belongs at Gate A

items.text: Agents were modelled without their own identity, and coops with members.
An audit leaned on summaries instead of primary sources.

problem.baseline: Ten corrections by Samuel Andert in the session's first 67 commits to theOS (31 Oct to 1 Nov 2026), before AIP-1's first spec, outside any gate: 1.5 per 10 commits. Seven were escapes, problems in work already called done (four layout, three sweeps); three were judgement.
whys: Samuel catches problems the agent should have caught. Why? The agent checks its own work, and only what it thinks of.
Why? Nothing independent checks the work against what a person sees, and nothing says beforehand what must be true.
Root cause: nothing independent checks the work against what a person sees, and nothing says beforehand what must be true.
problem.whys_note: The first draft went two whys further (the process lives in chat; there is no record). The zoom-out review showed that none of the ten came from lost context: those two whys described the planned solution, not the cause. They were removed.
truths: A language model is not deterministic; programs and proofs are.

Content that can't be reached is visible to a headless browser; a renamed word with one meaning is visible to a text search; a squeezed column or a stretched chip is visible in a screenshot to a fresh eye.
A checker that shares the author's context tends to agree with it.
A cloud container is reclaimed; only what is committed and pushed survives.
Git keeps every version and who made it.
assumptions: theOS is a standalone, fresh project: everything lives in theOS/, built from scratch. avenCEO touches no code outside theOS/. theOS owns avenSANDBOX (AIP-2) and its release (AIP-5); taking them over is their work.

theOS/ is the single source of truth and our memory: one JSON doc per thing. Three apps show them: Docs (theOS/docs/index.html, with the OLD-AIPs board), Intents (theOS/avenCEO/index.html) and Sources (theOS/sources/index.html), behind the dashboard theOS/index.html.

The plan adds, all inside theOS/: theOS/CLAUDE.md with the done rule, theOS/package.json with its lockfile (Playwright pinned to avenSANDBOX's image, the only source of the browser; until AIP-2 puts the check inside it, the session's Playwright and Chromium), and theOS/avenCEO/checks/ (the check command, the crawl and the docs check).
The 91 OLD-AIPs and their board are legacy: learned from; their decisions and lessons move into avenCEO's format in a later consolidation AIP.
Changes to the apps are ordinary edits under the done rule, not part of this AIP.
You pass Gate A and Gate B; machines pass the Mechanical gate and checkers the Review gate.
problem.risk: Can be undone: everything is files in git, inside theOS/; the done rule republishes a private artifact, undone by republishing the version before. No push to main, no deploy.

reuse.use: Used (theOS): the three apps read every doc by following its links; an AIP's stage is computed from its events.
Legacy (Samuel, 1 Nov): learned from; its decisions and lessons move into avenCEO's format when they are consolidated.
theOS owns avenSANDBOX from now on (D-24). The checks run in the session's box, with its Chromium and Playwright, until AIP-2 gives theOS its own.
Learned from, not touched: what a check of a hash-routed docs app checks (every view draws, no sideways scroll, wide tables in their own box, contrast, minimum slide text, a screenshot per view).
Learned from, not touched: the format for decided renames (→ x), words with two meanings (⚠) and their scopes. In theOS a rename is a term doc that supersedes the old word (D-18).
Learned from, not touched: its no-page-scroll rule fits /app, not theOS/docs, where a phone page scrolls by design.
Learned from, not touched: pick the checks a change needs from its paths.
Learned from, not touched: an append-only check compares a log with its earlier version.
Learned from, not touched: measure, change one thing, keep or revert, with a verdict.
Learned from, not touched: one claim checked with evidence lines; independent agents trying to refute a divergence.

claims.promise: The docs check fails at the parent of faf266961, where content could not be reached, and passes now.
claims.fails: It checks something a person does not see, or is tuned to the known bug.
claims.check: Its rule (every scroll container whose content is taller than it can scroll; the page never scrolls sideways; boxes made to scroll sideways are fine) is committed before the replay, then run at 390x844 and 1280x720: it fails at the parent of faf266961 in the one app there (theOS/docs), and passes on the current commit in the three apps.

claims.promise: The crawl reaches every state a person can reach from the HTML entry page it is given (theOS/index.html by default; theOS/docs/index.html on commits without a dashboard), following every link and button and dropping duplicate states: the same route with the same rendered text.
claims.fails: A state behind a button, or a renamed data file, is never seen.
claims.check: On the current commit it reaches every route the docs list (stories.json, intents.json, the index docs), and, in a test that starts at theOS/avenCEO/checks/fixtures/, a state planted behind a button; at the parents of 106ba0e5f and 3ddc07339 it reaches the OLD-AIP pages and their Learn tabs, with no edit per commit.

claims.promise: theOS's check command finishes in under 5 minutes for a change of one doc, so it is never the step that gets skipped.
claims.fails: The check is slow and is skipped.
claims.check: Timed in the session's box on a one-doc change with an empty cache (the box is reclaimed, so the cache lives only as long as the session); each screenshot taken after document.fonts.ready.

outcome.promise: Over the first three sessions after checkpoint 2 that change view code (.js, .css or .html), no content a person cannot reach and no page that scrolls sideways is ever called done.
outcome.how: The check runs on every change that touches view code; a correction of that kind is noted in the session doc, by hand.

gaps: The operations-shape sweep (one of the three sweeps) has no check; the pixel-diff checker may catch it, nothing promises it.
Running theOS's check command is part of the done rule, not enforced: enforcement is the deferred Stop hook.
The published artifact not updated after a change: no check; the done rule asks for it.
Renamed words: AIP-3's c6; until then the done rule's sweep, which nothing enforces.
done_rule: A change to theOS is done when theOS's check command is green (the crawl and the docs check), a decision that renames a word has been swept for the old word, it is pushed to the work branch, and the theOS artifact (a private claude.ai page, republished by avenMAIA with its files) is republished, its version noted in the commit message. In theOS, the repository's root check (aven/ops/devx/check.mjs) does not apply. The pixel diff and the look checker join it with AIP-6.
aip_when: An AIP is opened for work that needs your Gate A: a decision about what must be true (architecture, product behaviour, how we work). Small edits follow the done rule only.
mockup: The check's report: each app, its states, pass or fail; a folder of screenshots

checkpoints.adds: theOS/CLAUDE.md with the done rule (the root check does not apply in theOS; a decision that renames a word is swept for the old word); theOS/package.json and its lockfile; the check command with a crawl that follows links, and the docs check, which fails first at faf266961's parent. The undo of a republish (the version before) is tried once.
The crawl follows buttons too; the test page in theOS/avenCEO/checks/fixtures/; a screenshot of every state at 390x844 and 1280x720; the check's time limit.

deferred.until: Three intents were run by hand and escapes remain.
Agents are measured stopping early. Then: only on branches with an open record, honouring stop_hook_active, never blocking on Gate A or B.

deferred.what: Consolidating the 91 current intents into this format
deferred.until: A later AIP (Samuel, 1 Nov: "we consolidate the current AIPs later into the new flow format"). Their decisions have no claims or checkpoints yet, so that AIP decides how each maps.

deferred.what: Memory: decisions and their reflection, terms, the trace, authors, the schema of every doc
Release gating, and where theOS's checks run

deleted: Anything in legacy code: rules in the repository's check.mjs, entries in aven/ops/ci/suites.json, agents in the repository's .claude, a line in its CLAUDE.md. theOS is standalone (D-4); taking over the release pipeline is AIP-5's, not this one's (D-24).
Choosing which views the checker sees: the pixel diff chooses.
Picking checks by path: theOS is small, and every check always runs.
Contrast and slide text size: no escape asked for them.
The memory and decision-history section: it moved to AIP-3, brain (D-25).
The terms check: it moved to AIP-3 (c6), where a term carries its old word and scope.
The 1440x900 size: no escape needed it.
